transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-04-02 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nadar (Lunaris Head of Platform), Tom Bowers (ML Infra), Samira Khan (Finance)

Auto-summary (auto):
Maya and Diego walked Lunaris through the Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted economics, VPC/SOC2 requirements, KV cache benefits, and rollout strategies. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing + route-level examples.

Topics covered:
- Console: route dashboards, token-level cost, anomaly detection
- Routing/policy: automatic fallback, dedicated pools, burst capacity
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
- Optimize: batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization recommendations

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're sorted to demo the inference ops dashboard and how you can map costs back to routes, uh, use cases. 
[00:18] Priya Nadar: Thanks Maya, excited to see it. Quick context: we run multitenant agents for our field robots, about 3k token avg per session, and peaks up to 120 qps during test windows. We're trying to understand economics before committing to dedicated capacity.
[00:37] Diego Alvarez: Got it. I'll go through the route-level dashboards then show how Optimize recommends batching and quantization profiles. Quick question on tenancy — do you need full VPC private plane or is customer-managed network enough?
[00:52] Tom Bowers: We need VPC and KMS; some of our telemetry is regulated, so we also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also we need SSO (SAML).
[01:05] Maya Chen: Yep that's supported. For Private deployments we ship a control plane you can run in your VPC or on-prem, and key material can stay in your KMS/HSM. We'll send SOC2 artifacts — sorry, our compliance pack — after the call.
[01:20] Samira Khan: From finance perspective, we need to see per-route cost attribution — not just tokens but also infra overhead, idle GPU cost, etc. How precise is that?
[01:36] Diego Alvarez: Great question. The Console shows per-route token count, per-token inference cost, plus allocation of reserved capacity amortized across routes. There's also a tunable overhead mapping for idle time and autoscale buffers. It's not exact to the cent but within expected accounting margins for pilots.
[01:56] Priya Nadar: Can you show an example?
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: Sure let me share screen — here's the usage map. You can see routes on the left, top consumers highlighted, cost per 1k tokens in the middle. For your traffic patterns, prefix/KV cache can cut repeated-system prompt cost a lot — especially for telemetry parsing flows.
[02:28] [Screen share: Console -> Usage Analytics -> Routes] 
[02:37] Diego Alvarez: If you click into a route, we show token distribution, latency percentiles, cost per minute, and a cost waterfall: model cost, GPU amortized, network, and reserved pool overhead. The waterfall helps finance reconcile variance.
[02:58] Tom Bowers: That waterfall looks useful. How do you compute amortized GPU — is it based on reserved instances or on actual usage?
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: It's configurable. By default we use reserved capacity amortization, i.e., committed GPU cost spread across routes based on allocation shares. But you can switch to usage-based allocation which uses actual active minutes for each route.
[03:25] Maya Chen: For Dedicated customers we usually recommend reserved amortization to give predictable unit economics; for Hosted pilot teams usage based is often more accurate for short runs.
[03:37] Priya Nadar: We're worried about tail latencies at 120 qps; do you have per-region and per-model percentiles?
[03:47] Diego Alvarez: Yes, per-route breakdowns include p50/p95/p99 latency by model and region. Also you can pin model variants for a route and have automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if latency SLOs can't be met.
[04:03] Samira Khan: Fallback sounds risky for quality. How do you surface when fallback happens?
[04:11] Diego Alvarez: The Console flags fallback events and shows before/after output samples if you enable output logging (customer-enabled). For regulated workloads you can turn output logging off and rely on metadata only.
[04:25] [05:00] Maya Chen: Let's walk through an example economics scenario — hosted vs dedicated at your 120 qps peak with 3k tokens average. 
[05:11] Diego Alvarez: Rough ballpark: hosted cost per 1k tokens with our curated open models at that scale is X (we'll put numbers in the follow-up deck), dedicated reserved capacity can reduce unit cost by ~30-45% depending on quantization and batching.
[05:29] Tom Bowers: Does that assume you can use quantized kernels on our model? We run a slightly modified Llama fork.
[05:39] Diego Alvarez: We model compatibility; most of the Llama variants we've onboarded run with 4-bit quantization and optimized kernels. There are edge cases where ops differ; we run a quick compatibility test during onboarding. That's part of the benchmark Diego will run.
[05:53] Priya Nadar: What's the effort to try Private vs Dedicated — timeline wise?
[06:01] Maya Chen: For Dedicated reserved pools we can go from contract to live in 2–4 weeks if infra access is available. Private (VPC) onboarding typically takes 4–8 weeks due to networking and compliance checks.
[06:14] Samira Khan: On compliance, do you provide SOC2 Type II docs and pen test results?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO artifacts are in our compliance pack; pen test summaries we can provide under NDA. We'll drop the compliance link in Slack.
[06:33] [06:45] Diego Alvarez: Jumping back to Optimize features — the system suggests batching windows and KV cache TTLs based on your latency SLOs. For example, with your 3k token sessions we might set batch window at 15ms for interactive flows and 80ms for background summarization routes.
[07:05] Tom Bowers: How much does batching save?
[07:10] Diego Alvarez: It depends on request size distribution, but we've seen 20–60% cost reductions on token-heavy routes. With prefix caching for repeated system context you can see additional reductions.
[07:24] Priya Nadar: You mentioned prefix/KV cache — is that per-route or global? How do you handle cache invalidation?
[07:33] Diego Alvarez: We allow per-route cache policies and a shared KV cache option for related routes. Invalidation can be TTL-based or explicit via API. We also support warm-starting KV caches during canary rollouts.
[07:48] Samira Khan: From procurement I need clear reporting for chargeback. Does Console export per-route cost breakdown for our billing systems?
[07:58] Maya Chen: Yes, exports available as CSV or S3 export. We can provide a mapping that matches your chargeback fields. I'll include a sample CSV in the follow-up.
[08:10] [08:30] Priya Nadar: On SLA — what latency/uptime commits do you typically hit for Dedicated?
[08:36] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with an SLA tailored in the contract; standard is 99.9% uptime and latency targets that depend on model/instance size. We'll scope SLOs in the pilot.
[08:48] Tom Bowers: Any known limits on model size for VPC/on-prem? We run a 70B shard for fine-tuning.
[08:57] Diego Alvarez: On-prem limits are primarily GPU memory. Our runtime supports model parallel and sharded KV cache but for extreme sizes we recommend dedicated multi-GPU clusters; we can provide an on-prem sizing guide.
[09:12] [09:30] Priya Nadar: Who's the escalation contact for security incidents?
[09:35] Maya Chen: We'll include a security contact and SLAs for incident response in the security docs; usually your CISO team will have a direct channel to our security ops.
[09:46] Samira Khan: Let's talk billing terms — are reserved pools billed monthly or yearly? Any discounts for annual commits?
[09:56] Maya Chen: Both options supported. Annual commits generally get better pricing and priority for capacity in our regions. We'll outline pricing tiers in the proposal.
[10:10] Diego Alvarez: Ok I'm going to show a quick demo of a route anomaly — here the anomaly detection flagged a sudden spike in per-token cost, likely due to an increase in average prompt length. You can set thresholds and auto-notify Slack or PagerDuty.
[10:30] [10:45] Diego Alvarez: Also showing per-route debug traces — these are optional and you control retention. They help SEs debug why latency spiked; for privacy you can redact outputs.
[11:00] Priya Nadar: We like the Slack/PagerDuty hooks. Can we attach runbooks to anomalous events?
[11:07] Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can attach an ops playbook to an alert. We also support canned runbooks for common incidents like model OOMs or KV cache thrash.
[11:20] Samira Khan: For the pilot, we need a cost projection spreadsheet that shows hosted baseline vs dedicated 3-month/12-month commit scenarios.
[11:30] Maya Chen: We'll prepare that. Diego will also run a throughput benchmark with your prompts to give realistic latency and token cost numbers.
[11:40] Tom Bowers: One small thing — does Redwood support on-the-fly quantization profiles per route?
[11:47] Diego Alvarez: You can assign quantization profiles per route; the runtime supports hot-swapping to a quantized variant but we're careful with warmup to avoid accuracy regressions. The Console surfaces model quality checks during any swap.
[11:59] [12:15] Priya Nadar: We'd love to test the KV cache on our telemetry parsing route, that should show big savings.
[12:24] Diego Alvarez: Perfect candidate. We'll instrument it in the bench and show before/after cost latency.
[12:33] Samira Khan: What information should I provide to procurement to speed PO?
[12:38] Maya Chen: If you can share the procurement contact, PO template, and expected billing entity we'll align terms. We'll also attach standard contract redlines we accept.
[12:49] Priya Nadar: I'll send procurement contact after this call.
[12:52] [13:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap — next steps: pricing + sample CSV, Diego to run bench, Lunaris to share traffic data, schedule workshop. Any other questions?
[13:14] Tom Bowers: One last technical ask — can the benchmark include an isolated test for KV cache warm-start time?
[13:21] Diego Alvarez: Yep we'll include warm-start and cold-start scenarios and show kv miss rates.
[13:28] Samira Khan: From finance I'll need the cost projection in both USD and our local functional currency.
[13:34] Maya Chen: Noted, we'll include both.
[13:38] [14:00] Priya Nadar: Thanks, that's helpful.
[14:05] Maya Chen: Great, thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed pilot timeline.
[14:12] [End of recording]
